ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the graph of the linear function $y=x+2$ intersects with the graph of $y=kx+b$ $(k\ne 0)$ at point $P$. What is the solution to the system of linear equations in two variables $\begin{cases}y=x+2\\ y=kx+b\end{cases}$ for $x$ and $y$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Observing the graph, we find: The graph of the linear function $y=x+2$ intersects with the graph of $y=kx+b \ (k \neq 0)$ at point P(1,3), \\
$\therefore$ the solution to the system of linear equations $\begin{cases}y=x+2\\ y=kx+b\end{cases}$ is $\boxed{\begin{cases}x=1\\ y=3\end{cases}}$.
